Section B
Answer any three questions.
Each question is introduced by stimulus material. In your answer you may refer to this material and/or
to other examples that you have studied.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define foreign exchange rate.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain two reasons why the value of a country’s exports may be greater than the value of its
imports.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Analyse how an increase in income tax can affect a country’s inflation rate.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Discuss whether or not governments should aim for a high rate of economic growth.

text: Australia’s foreign exchange rate fluctuates. The value of Australia’s exports is regularly greater
than the value of its imports. Australia is Papua New Guinea’s main trading partner. In 2019, the
government of Papua New Guinea increased income tax to reduce its inflation rate. It used other
policy measures to increase its economic growth rate.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify two influences on what products a person buys.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain two ways a government could decrease the consumption of demerit goods.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Analyse why workers may join a trade union.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Discuss whether or not tertiary sector workers are paid more than primary sector workers.

text: Trade union membership is much higher in Sweden than in most countries. In 2019, 70%
of Swedish workers were members of a trade union. More than 85% of Swedish workers are
employed in the tertiary sector, compared with only 2% in the primary sector. Swedish workers
spend their incomes on a variety of products some of which, e.g. sweets, are demerit goods.
Sweden has the 7 highest per head consumption of sweets in the world.
